chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have been narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'They speak the truth.' I said: 'And how is it that his prayer is not counted for forty mornings, neither less than that nor more?'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, measured the creation of man, so He made it a nutfah (drop) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it an 'alaqah (clot) for forty days. Then He transferred it and made it a mudghah (lump) for forty days.'
So when he drinks wine, it remains in his bone marrow (mushash) for forty days, according to the measure of the transition of his creation.'
He said, then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And similarly, all of his nourishment, his eating and drinking, remains in his bone marrow for forty days.'
ai.seo_question: Why are prayers not counted for forty days after drinking wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical rationale behind the forty-day period during which prayers are not accepted for one who consumes wine. He draws a profound parallel between the spiritual impurity caused by wine and the physical stages of human embryonic development, noting that the substance's essence lingers in the bone marrow (*mushash*) for forty days, mirroring the three forty-day phases of creation described in the Quran. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that physical consumption directly impacts the spiritual receptivity of the body, linking physiological reality with ritual validity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Al Husayn Bin Khalid who said, 
‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We are reporting from the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who drinks the wine, his Prayer would not be Counted for him for forty days’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They speak the truth’. I said, ‘And how come his Prayer would not be counted for forty days, neither less from that, nor more?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Measured the creation of the human being, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Caused his seed to be such for forty days. Then Transformed it, so it became a clot for forty days. Then Transformed it, so it became a lump for forty days.

So he, when he drinks the wine, it remains in his bone joints for forty days upon the measurement of his Creation’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And similar to that for the entirety of his food intake, and his drinks, they remain in his bone-joints for forty days’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu Nasr from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, Alayhi al-Salam, ‘It is narrated to us from the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, that he has said, “If one drinks wine his Salat (prayer) is not counted for forty days.’”
He (the Imam) said, ‘They have spoken the truth.’ I then asked, ‘How is it that his Salat (prayer) is not counted for forty days: no less and no more?’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, determined the creation of human beings so it becomes nutfah (seed, sperm) in forty days, then it changes and becomes a clot of blood in forty days, then it changes and becomes a lump of flesh (embryo) in forty days.
If he drinks wine it remains in his bone joints for forty days proportionate to the changes in his creation.’
He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) then said, ‘In the same away all of his other food and drinks remain in his bone joints for forty days.’”
